newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank seen dumping mortgage securities.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank seen dumping mortgage securities.

text.p: NationsBank Corp unloaded about $1.0 billion of mortgage-backed securities on Friday and is expected to continue liquidating mortgage paper in the coming days, traders and analysts said.
Traders said they expected the bank to continue selling securities as it adjusted its balance sheet after acquiring Boatmens Bancshares Inc last August.
"I would assume they likely aren't done," one mortgage analyst said.
Another analyst said he expected NationsBank to sell several billion dollars more, perhaps in commercial mortage-backeds.

Friday's bid list of adjustable-rate mortgage-backed securities (ARMs) came on the heels of NationsBank's sale of approximately $800 million in COFIs (mortgages pegged to the Federal Home Loan Bank's cost of funds index) and Government National Mortgage Association (Ginnie Mae) paper last week, traders said.
"Today, (the ARMs) traded very aggressively," said Michael Hoeh, senior portfolio manager at The Dreyfus Corp.
He said the market quickly digested the offer despite the fact that "there are positions in dealers' inventories that have been sitting for a while -- that are a lot cheaper."
One dealer in particular eagerly bid the bank's securities, many traders said.
Goldman Sachs & Co dealers "were agressive on the bid" and gobbled up the entire chunk in a one-block purchase, said one.
Hoeh noted that the offer did not depress the ARMs market, which generally would have reacted first.
"(ARMs) have been very firm and have really kept up with their durations this afternoon," he said.
Additionally, traders said they were impressed with NationsBank's timing and strategy.
"These guys have got great execution for that type of size," said one regional mortgage-backed trader.
"I'd be happy with that execution for a deal half that size," he said.
